title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #204
gist: A late-July 2026 link roundup themed on physical AI: Enigma's $71M seed and public robot-teleoperation stunt, Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 whole-body model family, DoorDash's FAA Part 135 drone certification, Zoox's first US approval for a steering-wheel-free robotaxi, and OpenAI giving 10,000 researchers free frontier-model access. McCormick's connective thesis is that competitive self-interest — commoditizing complements and counter-positioning against Anthropic — is currently producing public goods.

insights.claim: Robotics startup Enigma emerged from stealth with a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, an unusually large seed for a company with no shipped hardware.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Seed rounds of this size in robot foundation models signal that VC is treating robot training data as the next scarce input after web text.
insights.quote: emerging from stealth on Monday with a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital
insights.locator: (1) Enigma Comes Out of Stealth with $71M

insights.claim: Enigma opened more than 100 real AI-powered robot arms in Israel and California for anyone to control in real time through a browser at robots.online, turning public teleoperation into both a data-collection engine and a marketing stunt.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A cheap, orthogonal route to robot training data — watch whether crowd-sourced human-robot interaction beats capital-intensive teleop farms.
insights.quote: If the race in robotics is about accumulating real training data fast and cost-efficiently, this is a novel and orthogonal approach to that which doubles as a unique marketing stunt.
insights.locator: Enigma is building robot-agnostic software

insights.claim: Enigma's bet is that observing how ordinary humans naturally try to command machines — via text, audio, and demonstrations — yields both better robot interfaces and potentially a different kind of robotic brain.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If interface data proves as valuable as motion data, robot value could accrue to software layers rather than hardware OEMs.
insights.locator: Its bet is that studying how humans engage with robots

insights.claim: Enigma's founders Jonathan Jacobi and Gal Niv are not roboticists — they met in teenage hacking competitions and served in Israel's Unit 8200 — and McCormick argues that lack of a robotics PhD is an advantage because deep-tech researchers get locked into their dissertation path.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A reusable screen for deep-tech diligence: outsider founders can be a feature, not a red flag, in fields with entrenched research orthodoxy.
insights.quote: in deep tech, people can often get stuck in whichever path they focused on for their PhD. No PhD, no stuck.
insights.locator: Part of the reason the company is able

themes.theme: Gemini Robotics 2 and the one-model robot stack

insights.claim: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2 as three models — a vision-language-action model, an embodied-reasoning model for long-horizon planning and multi-robot coordination, and an on-device model — collapsing perception, planning, control, adaptation, safety, and collaboration into one family.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Vertical consolidation of the robot software stack under one lab compresses the addressable surface for point-solution robotics startups.
insights.quote: one model family handling perception, planning, control, adaptation, safety, and collaboration across different bodies
insights.locator: (2) Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Whole-Body Intelligence

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 can adapt to an entirely new robot body with a few hours of data, typically fewer than 200 examples, a sample-efficiency level that undercuts the assumption that each new embodiment requires a bespoke data campaign.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Low adaptation cost per embodiment erodes the moat of proprietary robot datasets and favors hardware commoditization.
insights.quote: a local model that can adapt to new robot bodies with a few hours of data, typically fewer than 200 examples
insights.locator: The release includes three models

insights.claim: DeepMind says the same model checkpoint controlled multiple embodiments including Apptronik's Apollo humanoid variants and a Franka Duo setup, with the humanoid walking, crouching, reaching, and manipulating in cluttered environments using both five-fingered hands and two-finger grippers.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Cross-embodiment generalization from a single checkpoint is the key technical unlock investors should track for humanoid capex to make sense.
insights.quote: DeepMind says the same model checkpoint controlled multiple embodiments, including Apollo variants and a Franka Duo setup.
insights.locator: With these models, GDM is moving beyond tabletop

insights.claim: Despite the Gemini Robotics 2 release, humanoid robots remain unsolved — movement speed still needs work and benchmarks show uneven multi-finger dexterity — so McCormick says Travis Kalanick's skepticism is 'still right, for now.'
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An optimist source explicitly flagging dexterity and speed gaps is a useful check on humanoid-robot valuation timelines.
insights.quote: Humanoid robots haven’t been solved yet. Travis Kalanick is still right, for now.
insights.locator: Humanoid robots haven’t been solved yet

themes.theme: DoorDash Air and commoditizing your complements

insights.claim: DoorDash Labs earned FAA Part 135 air carrier certification and launched DoorDash Air, making DoorDash only the eighth drone operator in the US to hold that certification.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Part 135 is a scarce regulatory asset; holding one of only eight puts DoorDash ahead of rivals on drone-delivery optionality.
insights.quote: Part 135 lets DoorDash operate as an air carrier, and the company says it is only the eighth drone operator to earn it.
insights.locator: (3) DoorDash Announces DoorDash Air Drones

insights.claim: DoorDash's strategy is that it already owns the defensible layer — the network of customers and merchants plus the coordination technology — and can therefore commoditize the transport layer, picking whichever modality sits at the right point on the cheap/fast Pareto frontier.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Frames DoorDash as a demand-and-coordination monopoly rather than a logistics operator — margin accrues to the network, not the vehicles.
insights.quote: they believer that it already owns the most important part of the delivery ecosystem - the network of customers and merchants and the technology to coordinate it all - and that it can commoditize the ways that it gets things from one party to the other.
insights.locator: The company’s strategy and bet is clear here

insights.claim: McCormick reads DoorDash's drones as a template to set standards and encourage competition among drone makers rather than a standalone drone business — the same commoditize-your-complements logic he ascribes to Nvidia and Microsoft signing the open-weights letter.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: One mental model — commoditize your complements — explains both big-tech open-weights advocacy and DoorDash's drone push; use it to predict who open-sources next.
insights.quote: Like Nvidia and Microsoft signing the letter, DoorDash is trying to commoditize its complements.
insights.locator: Someone smarter on drones than I am

insights.claim: DoorDash building its own drones echoes Uber's failed attempt to build its own self-driving cars; Uber abandoned that and now serves as a 'demand cannon' for dedicated AV makers, which is the precedent risk for DoorDash Air.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Base rate suggests aggregators end up distributing others' hardware; watch for DoorDash to pivot from building drones to routing demand to them.
insights.quote: It’s interesting to note that Uber is no longer doing that, but that it is providing a demand cannon to dedicated AV makers.
insights.locator: It’s a super interesting bet, like Uber trying

insights.claim: The most-liked reply to DoorDash's drone announcement was hostile 'dystopia' backlash, indicating consumer acceptance — not technology or regulation — may be the binding constraint on drone delivery.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Social license risk is an underpriced input to physical-AI rollout timelines even after FAA approval clears.
insights.quote: So we have a little ways to go before people get used to a burrito landing in their yard.
insights.locator: And look, I think it’s cool, but the most-liked reply

themes.theme: Zoox and the purpose-built AV form factor

insights.claim: Amazon's Zoox won US regulatory approval for limited commercial deployment of steering-wheel-free robotaxis, the first such approval in the autonomous ride industry per Reuters.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Regulatory precedent for driverless-by-design vehicles opens a new vehicle category distinct from retrofitted Waymo/Tesla fleets.
insights.quote: Zoox unit won ​U.S. approval on Wednesday for limited commercial deployment of its novel steering-wheel-free robotaxis, a first for the autonomous ride industry
insights.locator: (4) Zoox Wins 1st US Approval for Robotaxis

insights.claim: Zoox matters not as the first self-driving car — Waymo and Tesla already operate in multiple US markets — but as the first ground-up commercial vehicle designed for a world with no human driver, with no driver's seat and two rows of inward-facing seats.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Distinguishes retrofit AV economics from clean-sheet vehicle design; the latter changes automotive supply chains and interior suppliers, not just software.
insights.quote: the Adam or Eve of future generations of vehicles that never even contemplated that a human might drive it
insights.locator: This isn’t the first self-driving car, obviously

insights.claim: McCormick predicts cars will increasingly be designed as 'moving rooms' where riders work, watch movies, or receive services in transit, implying in-vehicle experience becomes a monetizable surface.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Points to a new in-transit attention/services market layered on top of AV ride economics.
insights.quote: I would imagine that in the future, cars will be designed more and more like moving rooms.
insights.locator: In Zoox’s case, that means no driver’s seat

insights.claim: McCormick argues physical-world AI — how people and things move — is both cooler and materially more underappreciated than computer-based AI that currently absorbs the market's attention.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An explicit steer toward embodied-AI exposure (AVs, drones, robots) as the mispriced leg of the AI trade versus software AI.
insights.quote: I continue to think that the way cooler and way more underappreciated thing is what’s going to happen in the physical world, and in particular the way that we move people and things
insights.locator: Everyone is super excited about computer AI

insights.claim: OpenAI is giving free frontier-model access to 10,000 scientists, mathematicians, and engineers via ChatGPT for Academic Researchers, expanding to 100,000 through 2027.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Free frontier access at academic scale is both a distribution land-grab in R&D workflows and a moat-builder against vertical AI entrants.
insights.quote: We’re giving scientists, mathematicians, and engineers free access to our frontier models—starting with 10,000 researchers and expanding to 100,000 through 2027.
insights.locator: (5) OpenAI Gives 10k Researchers Free Access

insights.claim: The dominant competitive dynamic McCormick sees in AI right now is market incentives aligning almost everyone against the perceived market leader Anthropic, pushing rivals toward actions that benefit everyone else.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Treats Anthropic as the incumbent target — the coalition dynamic (open weights, free access) is a structural headwind to Anthropic's pricing and positioning.
insights.quote: market incentives aligning almost everyone against the market leader, Anthropic, and towards things that are great for everyone else
insights.locator: There’s almost nothing I’ve found as fascinating

insights.claim: OpenAI's messaging shift — AI as a tool that empowers people rather than a system that replaces them or predicts the future — is deliberate counter-positioning against Anthropic's more opinionated risk-forward stance, designed to deflate replacement fears and make Anthropic look weird.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Narrative positioning is now a competitive weapon in AI; brand/comms strategy is a tradeable differentiator between labs.
insights.quote: The whole thing is designed to deflate fears that AI will replace us and to make Anthropic look weird.
insights.locator: Basically, OpenAI’s new message since bringing

insights.claim: McCormick reads the free-researcher program as a specific counter to Anthropic going vertical in categories like biotech — arming external scientists is cheaper than building the vertical yourself.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If labs answer vertical integration with horizontal free distribution, vertical AI application startups face a subsidized-tooling squeeze.
insights.quote: counter-positioning against Anthropic trying to go more vertical in certain categories like biotech means that OpenAI is giving free frontier models to tens of thousands of researchers
insights.locator: What’s amazed me most this week

insights.claim: McCormick cautions that OpenAI's tool-not-master rhetoric and open-letter signature are words, while the company is likely lobbying behind the scenes for regulatory capture at the same time.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Discount public AI-policy positioning from labs; watch actual lobbying disclosures for where rule-setting advantage is being sought.
insights.quote: But those are words, as is signing the open letter, and at the same time, OpenAI is likely lobbying behind the scenes for regulatory capture, too.
insights.locator: But those are words, as is signing the open letter

insights.claim: The broader lesson McCormick draws is a defense of capitalism in AI: even where you distrust the actors, competitive incentives push companies to produce publicly beneficial outputs like free research tooling and open-weight advocacy.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Predicts more public-good releases from AI labs as a byproduct of rivalry — a deflationary force on paid AI tooling in research niches.
insights.quote: even if you don’t trust Sam or OpenAI or big tech, companies are incentivized to do things that are good for the public, too
insights.locator: What’s amazed me most this week, and made me appreciate capitalism

insights.claim: Big tech companies came out in favor of open-weight models out of pure self-interest, a dynamic McCormick argues supports viewing AI as a commodity input ('oil') rather than a singular transformative agent ('god').
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The oil-not-god frame implies AI margins compress toward infrastructure economics, favoring complement owners over model owners.
insights.quote: the big tech companies came out in favor of open-weight models out of pure self-interest, which I wrote about in AI is Oil, Not God.
insights.locator: We sent the Dose last Friday morning

insights.claim: General Catalyst, per McCormick's conversation with CEO Hemant Taneja around the firm's Q2 letter, owns a healthcare system outright and has made Anthropic its biggest position.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A top allocator concentrating its largest position in Anthropic while owning operating assets shows VC morphing into hybrid operator-investor structures.
insights.quote: including owning a healthcare system and making Anthropic its biggest position
insights.locator: (Extra 1) My Conversation with General Catalyst CEO

insights.claim: McCormick notes very few firms are deploying more capital in more different ways into AI in private markets than General Catalyst, framing it as a bellwether for how private AI capital is being structured.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Track GC's structures (buyouts, healthcare ownership, concentrated model bets) as a leading indicator of where private AI capital flows next.
insights.quote: there are very few firms deploying more capital in more different ways to AI in the private markets than General Catalyst
insights.locator: There is a ton going on in the private markets
